question.problem:
The entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in the inverse of the matrix

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 \\ k & -2 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

equals $-2.$ Find the value of $k.$

$k=${{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the determinant of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 \\ k & -2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}|-(-2)|\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ k & -1\end{aligned}|+(-2)|\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ k & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)((-1)(-1)-(-2)(-2))+2((-2)(-1)-(-2)k)+(-2)((-2)(-2)-(-1)k) \\  & =(-2)(1-4)+2(2+2k)+(-2)(4+k) \\  & =6+4+4k-8-2k \\  & =2k+2\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want the entry ${a}_{32}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{32}^{t}={c}_{23}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{23} & =(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ k & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-((-2)(-2)-(-2)k) \\  & =-(4+2k) \\  & =-2k-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{32}^{′} & =\frac{1}{det(A)}{c}_{32}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{det(A)}{c}_{23} \\  & =\frac{-2k-4}{2k+2} \\  & =-\frac{k+2}{k+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are told that ${a}_{32}^{′}=-2$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{k+2}{k+1} & =-2 \\ \frac{k+2}{k+1} & =2 \\ k+2 & =2k+2 \\ k & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
